Some rules have a second shape. A variant replaces the rule's phases for that move.

<!-- table: maneuver-variants -->
| Rule id | Variant | Length ms | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `objective.accomplish` | `beamed` | 5200 | The Story's merged work went to stations: each charges (0.6 s) and fires its mining beam over a 2.6 s act |
| `threat.accomplish` | `beamed` | 5600 | The Bug's merged fixes went to stations: each charges and fires its phaser over a 2.6 s act; the enemy ship blows apart under it |
| `attachment.merge` | `first` | 7900 | The facility's first merge in the round: the station transforms from the merge's gather (tell 300, gather 900, act 2300, land 500, echo 3000, disperse 900) and fires as the longest transformation (4.4 s) ends: 300 + 900 + 2300 + 500 + the 700 ms charge = 4700; it holds the facility, so nothing else casting it starts first (nothing else casting the station acts until it ends) |
| `objective.accomplish` | `short` | 2520 | (27 E4d, P7) The plain close at 0.6× (`SHORT_PACE`), its land kept at 1.2 s (`CLOSE_SLIDE_MS`). The director plays it (05 P-21, P-23) |
| `objective.accomplish` | `beamed-short` | 3600 | The beamed close at 0.6×, land kept at 1.2 s. Director's choice (05 P-21, P-23) |
| `threat.accomplish` | `short` | 3000 | The plain strike at 0.6×, land kept at 1.2 s. Director's choice (05 P-21, P-23) |
| `threat.accomplish` | `beamed-short` | 3840 | The beamed strike at 0.6×, land kept at 1.2 s. Director's choice (05 P-21, P-23) |
| `attachment.merge` | `short` | 4320 | A later merge at 0.6×. A *first* merge has no short form: it happens once per station and the transformation floors it. Director's choice (05 P-21, P-23) |
| `seat.complete` | `short` | 2400 | The homeworld bloom at 0.6×. Director's choice (05 P-21, P-23) |
| `region.clear` | `short` | 1770 | The all-clear at 0.6×. Director's choice (05 P-21, P-23) |

**Source:** `pace.ts` `variant` on each rule (`beamed`, and the merge's inline `first`) and `short` (`shortForm`: `short`, or `<variant>-short`) · **Guard:** `docTables.test.ts`, `maneuvers.test.ts`, gallery maneuver demos (each variant has its own cell) · **Update when:** a variant is added, renamed or retimed, or its condition changes.

**A volley (27 E6a, 05 M-31, B-21)** is not a variant: it plays its carrier's own form (full, `first` or `short`) with the members' union cast, and its echo lengthens so that each member's naming turn (`VOLLEY_TURN_MS`, 2540 ms) opens before the disperse: `disperse.atMs ≥ claim + turns × 2540`. A pair under the full Power link needs no stretch (1200 + 5080 ≤ 6300); under the short form (act at 720, disperse at 3780) a pair's echo grows by 2020 ms (echo 1800 → 3820, disperse 3780 → 5800). Its other members are `joined` and play nothing of their own.

A maneuver uses some of six phases, in this order. Every claimed look lands at the start of `land`,
or at the end of `act` when a rule has no `land`.

<!-- table: phases -->
| Phase | Means |
|---|---|
| `tell` | Draws the eye to where it will happen: usually a ring tightening on the spot |
| `gather` | The cast assembles: ships sortie out, a formation forms, light gathers |
| `act` | The change itself: beams, bolts, the art's own act (a break-up, a jump, a dock) |
| `land` | The new look lands; the payoff (the grand flare) |
| `echo` | The afterglow: a settle ring, a flare, a station's split beam |
| `disperse` | The cast goes home; a last faint ring |

**Source:** `src/shared/contracts/maneuver.ts` `PHASES`; land timing in `chart/fx/v1/interpreter.ts` · **Guard:** `docTables.test.ts`, `maneuvers.test.ts` · **Update when:** a phase is added or renamed, or the interpreter changes when looks land.

# Tests, and how to iterate quickly

**Status:** current as of 2026-10-27 (through v1.3 Block B). The e2e specs and goldens are named below, and the unit tests and
drive steps mostly are; the v1.2 tests and steps are listed in the v1 table's v1.2 rows.

Decided 2026-10-07: the full e2e suite takes minutes, so iteration runs a few of its pieces, and the
full suite runs once before handing back.

| Command | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `npm test` | Unit and golden (Vitest) | ~5 s |
| `npm run e2e:keystone` | One path per area, tagged `@keystone`, specs in parallel | ~40 s |
| `npm run e2e:spec -- <name…>` | Named specs, e.g. `npm run e2e:spec -- explore slice4` | per spec |
| `npm run e2e` | Everything: the specs in parallel, then the pixel and frame-time specs alone | ~3 min |
| `npm run bake:asteroids` | Re-bake `assets/atlas/asteroids.{png,json}` from the procedural asteroids through the gallery (23 C7); `asteroid-atlas.spec.ts` checks the atlas path renders (no missing frames) with its flag on | seconds |
| `npm run drive -- <steps.ts>` | Launch the app, run steps, keep screenshots, state, console, and dev log | seconds |

**While iterating:** run the specs for what changed (below), plus `e2e:keystone` once things look
right. Run `npm run e2e` once before handing work back.

## Windows don't appear (decided 2026-10-09)

`npm run e2e` never shows its windows: they were opening centred, over whatever you were doing. A
hidden window still animates (`backgroundThrottling` is off in test mode) and Playwright still
composites it, so the pixel baselines and the review stills are unaffected — the whole suite passes
hidden.

- **To watch a run:** `STAR_CHART_TEST_SHOW=1 npm run e2e` (or any single spec). The window is pinned
  to the top-left of the primary display, and opens without taking focus.
- **`STAR_CHART_TEST_DPR=2`** launches with that devicePixelRatio (default 1), for checks that depend on it.

input.content:
# F2 Summon on the fly: tests written ahead of the build

These tests were written before the build and fail on this tree (`bench`, after F1). Fixture data only (INV-18): the
renderer tests play pod-sprint's first summoned jump-in (Sprint 13) on a stub scene, and every invented key is
`wi:o:f2-next`.

## Acceptance → tests

| Acceptance line | Test (file › name) | Why it fails now |
|---|---|---|
| Unit test: the summoner's pursue has no hold between its flight and its next place | `tests/unit/summonOnTheFly.test.ts` › *with nothing waiting, it flies out, passes the station, and carries on to its rest with no hold on the way* | The real `Sortie` parks the ship at the spot for `holdS` (crew hold): it sits still for 3800 ms (allowed ≤ 60 ms) |
| … next sortie if waiting (E4's P4) | same file › *with its next sortie waiting (P4), it carries on from the spot to that sortie's place with no hold* | It parks at the jump-in spot for 3820 ms before the next sortie takes it |
| … the station's act starts within 50 ms of the blip; one call blip | same file › *gives one call blip as it passes, at the ship, and the station's act starts within 50 ms of it* | There's no blip: every ring the jump-in draws today sits on the station (`expected [] to have a length of 1`) |
| Decided: same hue and ring shape as the arrival (R8, R10) | same file › *the blip matches the arrival: the same hue and the same ring shape* | No blip to match |
| Decided: named from the blip, plate rides with the ship for `NOTE_MIN_MS` | same file › *the summoner is named from the blip, and its plate rides with the moving ship for NOTE_MIN_MS* | The plate opens at the act (that part passes), but the ship is parked while it shows: it travels 0 in that time |
| Decided: under reduced motion the ship doesn't fly; the blip and the arrival play at its place | same file › *under reduced motion the ship doesn't fly: the blip and the arrival play at its place* | The ship stays put (that part passes), but there's no blip |
| 15 §7's row and `docTables.test.ts`: phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival | same file › *its phases are the flight (gather, from 0) and the arrival (act, and at most its land): no tell, no echo or disperse* | The rule still opens with `tell` 300 |
| … the hold goes (the planner's turn) | same file › *the planned jump-in holds no turn after its work: its length is its phases, and its ship is let go as it passes (the blip)* | The planned `durationMs` is 4835, stretched by `crewTimes` (span 2815); `releaseOfPlay` is 4835, not the claim (1015) |
| … 15 §7's row | same file › *15 §7's facility.enter row gives the new length* | The row says 2815. `docTables.test.ts` already checks that the row matches the code; this test also requires the length to be under E1's 2815 |
| The ledger shows the saving per pod | `tests/unit/pacingBuilt.test.ts` › *F2, summon on the fly: rows on all seven pods …* | `BUILT` has no `F2` entry (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'Comet Pod', …(6) ]`) |
| A gallery demo cell (the jump-in cell), full and reduced motion, no console errors | `tests/e2e/gallery-summon.spec.ts` › *the jump-in cell: the summoner passes without stopping, and under reduced motion doesn't fly; no console errors (27 F2)* | The cell loops and clears today, but the new stats field `agentTravel` doesn't exist yet (`received undefined`) |
| The schedule goldens are updated and the packet names each change | Not written (that's the build's job; see *Goldens* below) | — |

`npm test`: 10 failures, all of them the F2 tests above; the other 1719 pass. `npm run typecheck` and `eslint` on the
new and edited test files are clean. `npm run e2e:spec -- gallery-summon` fails only on the missing hook field.

## Names the builder must match

- **Gallery demo stats** (`gallery/maneuverDemos.ts` `DemoStats`, for every demo, over its last finished loop):
  - `agentStillMs`: the longest time (ms) the cast's first agent's ship sat still between its first move and its last
    (0 if it never moved). Full motion.
  - `agentTravel`: how far (world units) that ship travelled in the last full-motion loop.
  - `reducedAgentTravel`: the same, for the last loop that ran in reduced motion from start to end.
  The spec needs `agentTravel > 0`, `agentStillMs ≤ 120` (a gallery frame is at most 100 ms), and
  `reducedAgentTravel < 1e-3`.
- **The ledger:** a `BUILT` entry with `id: 'F2'` in `scripts/pacing-built.ts`. It has rows for **all seven** pods
  (`resolvePods({ all: true })`, so Meteor is included: F1 says "F2 to F4 opt in"), each with `savedMs ≥ 0`, and
  Meteor's `savedMs > 0`. The committed `pacing-ledger.md` Built section has a `| F2 …` row for each pod, and
  `pacing-built.json` stays current (the existing test).
- No other new exports. The unit tests use existing public functions only: `planManeuvers`, `releaseOfPlay`,
  `claimMs`, `nearStartMs`, `workEndOf`, `gatherAtOf`, `NOTE_MIN_MS`, `spanMs`, the `ManeuverInterpreter` and its
  `crew()`, and the seed `pursue`/`hold` commands.

## Decisions taken (27's Decisions don't cover these)

1. **Phase shape.** "The flight plus the arrival" means `gather` (the flight) first, at 0, then `act` (the arrival).
   `land` may stay, since the settle could be part of the arrival. No `tell`, `echo` or `disperse`. The test doesn't fix
   the phase lengths. It only requires the total to be under 2815.
2. **The hold goes in the engine too.** A planned jump-in is not stretched by the crew hold:
   `durationMs === spanMs(phases)`. Its ship is released at the blip: `releaseOfPlay(m) === claimMs(m.phases)`, the
   act's start. `NOTE_MIN_MS` still holds the jump-in's place in the attention budget through `heldMs`, as before.
3. **What "the blip" is.** It's one `ring` command call (`cmd.ring`), not centred on the station, drawn at the
   passing ship (within half a station radius of where the ship is drawn when the ring is made). Under reduced motion
   it's drawn at the ship's rest. The station's `act` (`jump`) starts within 50 ms of it.
4. **"Same hue and ring shape".** At least one ring on the station, made within 50 ms of the jump act, has the same
   `color` and the same `r1 / r` as the blip. Its size may differ, since a ship is smaller than a station.
5. **"No hold".** The ship's drawn position never stays still for more than 60 ms (3 frames of 20 ms). This holds from
   its first move until it first reaches its next place:
   - with nothing waiting, its rest (`goalOf`);
   - with a P4 sortie waiting, where it's drawn at that sortie's act start.
   The test plays the waiting sortie at the planner's own `nearStartMs` start.
6. **"Plate rides with the ship".** The summoner's crew plate (`fx.crew()`) opens within 60 ms of the jump act and
   stays open at least `NOTE_MIN_MS` (allowing 40 ms of frame slack). During that time the ship travels more than one
   station radius and never parks for more than 60 ms.
7. **The jump-in cell** is the Maneuvers section's `facility.enter` demo (`[data-art="maneuvers:facility.enter"]`),
   not the station-art *Jump-in* cell in `gallery/v1/stations.ts`.
8. **`pacingBuilt`'s frozen-rows filter** (`E1 to E5 measure what they measured before volleys`) now also skips ids
   starting with `F`, so the new F2 rows don't break it.

## Hazards for the build (existing tests the change will move)

- `tests/unit/commands.test.ts` › *Station jump-in issues no beacon, bearing or planet rings…* reads the gather's
  single fold ring (a repeat) and the land's ring. Update it to the new choreography.
- `tests/unit/pacingBuilt.test.ts` `BEFORE_VOLLEYS` freezes E1's rows. E1's "now" run uses today's `facility.enter`,
  so F2 will move those rows, and E4a/E4c's too, if summons are on their critical paths. Undo F2 in the earlier
  items' runs (as E7, E8 and E10 do for theirs), or the frozen rows fail.
- `tests/unit/maneuvers.test.ts` › *an attachment opens once its facility has entered* (`afterMs: enter.durationMs`)
  should still pass with the shorter `durationMs`.
- `tests/unit/docTables.test.ts` §7: change 15 §7's `facility.enter` row (Length ms, What you see) with the code.

## Goldens expected to change (not regenerated here)

- `tests/golden/__golden__/director.json`: each pod's `estimateMs`, and possibly its `forms` and `climaxes`, since
  every pod has a summon.
- The committed ledger files `docs/progress/v1.4/pacing-ledger.{md,json}` and `pacing-built.json`
  (`npm run pacing -- --candidates`).
- Probably unchanged: the layout goldens (`*.plan.json`, `*.round.json`, `*.scenes.json`, including
  `halcyon-meteor.*`) and the v0 goldens (`*.schedule.json`, `*.seek.json`, `*.highlights.json`), which don't play
  Solar maneuvers. The packet should name any that move.

# F2 Summon on the fly: tests written ahead of the build

These tests were written before the build and fail on this tree (`bench`, after F1). Fixture data only (INV-18): the
renderer tests play pod-sprint's first summoned jump-in (Sprint 13) on a stub scene, and every invented key is
`wi:o:f2-next`.

## Acceptance → tests

| Acceptance line | Test (file › name) | Why it fails now |
|---|---|---|
| Unit test: the summoner's pursue has no hold between its flight and its next place | `tests/unit/summonOnTheFly.test.ts` › *with nothing waiting, it flies out, passes the station, and carries on to its rest with no hold on the way* | The real `Sortie` parks the ship at the spot for `holdS` (crew hold): it sits still for 3800 ms (allowed ≤ 60 ms) |
| … next sortie if waiting (E4's P4) | same file › *with its next sortie waiting (P4), it carries on from the spot to that sortie's place with no hold* | It parks at the jump-in spot for 3820 ms before the next sortie takes it |
| … the station's act starts within 50 ms of the blip; one call blip | same file › *gives one call blip as it passes, at the ship, and the station's act starts within 50 ms of it* | There's no blip: every ring the jump-in draws today sits on the station (`expected [] to have a length of 1`) |
| Decided: same hue and ring shape as the arrival (R8, R10) | same file › *the blip matches the arrival: the same hue and the same ring shape* | No blip to match |
| Decided: named from the blip, plate rides with the ship for `NOTE_MIN_MS` | same file › *the summoner is named from the blip, and its plate rides with the moving ship for NOTE_MIN_MS* | The plate opens at the act (that part passes), but the ship is parked while it shows: it travels 0 in that time |
| Decided: under reduced motion the ship doesn't fly; the blip and the arrival play at its place | same file › *under reduced motion the ship doesn't fly: the blip and the arrival play at its place* | The ship stays put (that part passes), but there's no blip |
| 15 §7's row and `docTables.test.ts`: phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival | same file › *its phases are the flight (gather, from 0) and the arrival (act, and at most its land): no tell, no echo or disperse* | The rule still opens with `tell` 300 |
| … the hold goes (the planner's turn) | same file › *the planned jump-in holds no turn after its work: its length is its phases, and its ship is let go as it passes (the blip)* | The planned `durationMs` is 4835, stretched by `crewTimes` (span 2815); `releaseOfPlay` is 4835, not the claim (1015) |
| … 15 §7's row | same file › *15 §7's facility.enter row gives the new length* | The row says 2815. `docTables.test.ts` already checks that the row matches the code; this test also requires the length to be under E1's 2815 |
| The ledger shows the saving per pod | `tests/unit/pacingBuilt.test.ts` › *F2, summon on the fly: rows on all seven pods …* | `BUILT` has no `F2` entry (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'Comet Pod', …(6) ]`) |
| A gallery demo cell (the jump-in cell), full and reduced motion, no console errors | `tests/e2e/gallery-summon.spec.ts` › *the jump-in cell: the summoner passes without stopping, and under reduced motion doesn't fly; no console errors (27 F2)* | The cell loops and clears today, but the new stats field `agentTravel` doesn't exist yet (`received undefined`) |
| The schedule goldens are updated and the packet names each change | Not written (that's the build's job; see *Goldens* below) | — |

`npm test`: 10 failures, all of them the F2 tests above; the other 1719 pass. `npm run typecheck` and `eslint` on the
new and edited test files are clean. `npm run e2e:spec -- gallery-summon` fails only on the missing hook field.

## Names the builder must match

- **Gallery demo stats** (`gallery/maneuverDemos.ts` `DemoStats`, for every demo, over its last finished loop):
  - `agentStillMs`: the longest time (ms) the cast's first agent's ship sat still between its first move and its last
    (0 if it never moved). Full motion.
  - `agentTravel`: how far (world units) that ship travelled in the last full-motion loop.
  - `reducedAgentTravel`: the same, for the last loop that ran in reduced motion from start to end.
  The spec needs `agentTravel > 0`, `agentStillMs ≤ 120` (a gallery frame is at most 100 ms), and
  `reducedAgentTravel < 1e-3`.
- **The ledger:** a `BUILT` entry with `id: 'F2'` in `scripts/pacing-built.ts`. It has rows for **all seven** pods
  (`resolvePods({ all: true })`, so Meteor is included: F1 says "F2 to F4 opt in"), each with `savedMs ≥ 0`, and
  Meteor's `savedMs > 0`. The committed `pacing-ledger.md` Built section has a `| F2 …` row for each pod, and
  `pacing-built.json` stays current (the existing test).
- No other new exports. The unit tests use existing public functions only: `planManeuvers`, `releaseOfPlay`,
  `claimMs`, `nearStartMs`, `workEndOf`, `gatherAtOf`, `NOTE_MIN_MS`, `spanMs`, the `ManeuverInterpreter` and its
  `crew()`, and the seed `pursue`/`hold` commands.

## Decisions taken (27's Decisions don't cover these)

1. **Phase shape.** "The flight plus the arrival" means `gather` (the flight) first, at 0, then `act` (the arrival).
   `land` may stay, since the settle could be part of the arrival. No `tell`, `echo` or `disperse`. The test doesn't fix
   the phase lengths. It only requires the total to be under 2815.
2. **The hold goes in the engine too.** A planned jump-in is not stretched by the crew hold:
   `durationMs === spanMs(phases)`. Its ship is released at the blip: `releaseOfPlay(m) === claimMs(m.phases)`, the
   act's start. `NOTE_MIN_MS` still holds the jump-in's place in the attention budget through `heldMs`, as before.
3. **What "the blip" is.** It's one `ring` command call (`cmd.ring`), not centred on the station, drawn at the
   passing ship (within half a station radius of where the ship is drawn when the ring is made). Under reduced motion
   it's drawn at the ship's rest. The station's `act` (`jump`) starts within 50 ms of it.
4. **"Same hue and ring shape".** At least one ring on the station, made within 50 ms of the jump act, has the same
   `color` and the same `r1 / r` as the blip. Its size may differ, since a ship is smaller than a station.
5. **"No hold".** The ship's drawn position never stays still for more than 60 ms (3 frames of 20 ms). This holds from
   its first move until it first reaches its next place:
   - with nothing waiting, its rest (`goalOf`);
   - with a P4 sortie waiting, where it's drawn at that sortie's act start.
   The test plays the waiting sortie at the planner's own `nearStartMs` start.
6. **"Plate rides with the ship".** The summoner's crew plate (`fx.crew()`) opens within 60 ms of the jump act and
   stays open at least `NOTE_MIN_MS` (allowing 40 ms of frame slack). During that time the ship travels more than one
   station radius and never parks for more than 60 ms.
7. **The jump-in cell** is the Maneuvers section's `facility.enter` demo (`[data-art="maneuvers:facility.enter"]`),
   not the station-art *Jump-in* cell in `gallery/v1/stations.ts`.
8. **`pacingBuilt`'s frozen-rows filter** (`E1 to E5 measure what they measured before volleys`) now also skips ids
   starting with `F`, so the new F2 rows don't break it.

## Names the builder must match

- **Gallery demo stats** (`gallery/maneuverDemos.ts` `DemoStats`, for every demo, over its last finished loop):
  - `agentStillMs`: the longest time (ms) the cast's first agent's ship sat still between its first move and its last

  - `agentTravel`: how far (world units) that ship travelled in the last full-motion loop.
  - `reducedAgentTravel`: the same, for the last loop that ran in reduced motion from start to end.
  The spec needs `agentTravel > 0`, `agentStillMs ≤ 120` (a gallery frame is at most 100 ms), and

## Decisions taken (27's Decisions don't cover these)

1. **Phase shape.** "The flight plus the arrival" means `gather` (the flight) first, at 0, then `act` (the arrival).

   the phase lengths. It only requires the total to be under 2815.
2. **The hold goes in the engine too.** A planned jump-in is not stretched by the crew hold:
   `durationMs === spanMs(phases)`. Its ship is released at the blip: `releaseOfPlay(m) === claimMs(m.phases)`, the
   act's start. `NOTE_MIN_MS` still holds the jump-in's place in the attention budget through `heldMs`, as before.
3. **What "the blip" is.** It's one `ring` command call (`cmd.ring`), not centred on the station, drawn at the
   passing ship (within half a station radius of where the ship is drawn when the ring is made). Under reduced motion
   it's drawn at the ship's rest. The station's `act` (`jump`) starts within 50 ms of it.

5. **"No hold".** The ship's drawn position never stays still for more than 60 ms (3 frames of 20 ms). This holds from

   - with nothing waiting, its rest (`goalOf`);
   - with a P4 sortie waiting, where it's drawn at that sortie's act start.
   The test plays the waiting sortie at the planner's own `nearStartMs` start.
6. **"Plate rides with the ship".** The summoner's crew plate (`fx.crew()`) opens within 60 ms of the jump act and

7. **The jump-in cell** is the Maneuvers section's `facility.enter` demo (`[data-art="maneuvers:facility.enter"]`),
   not the station-art *Jump-in* cell in `gallery/v1/stations.ts`.
8. **`pacingBuilt`'s frozen-rows filter** (`E1 to E5 measure what they measured before volleys`) now also skips ids

# F2 Summon on the fly: review 1

Reviewer: fresh, adversarial. Reviewed the uncommitted working-tree diff on `bench` against the tests in a985a15, the item
F2 (27), 02 §1, 13 §1 (R1–R14), 13 §6, 15 §7/§8/§10, 05 §8, tests.md and build.md. Fixture data only (INV-18).

## Verdict: **changes requested** (0 Blockers, 4 Majors, 5 Minors, 3 Nits)

The choreography does what the item asks. The pass has no hold, there's one blip at the passing ship with the station's
`jump` at the same instant, and the hue and `r1/r` match. Reduced motion plays both at the ship's rest. The engine no
longer stretches the jump-in by the crew hold. The edits to existing tests are justified. All checks pass. The problems:

- The plate is whole for less than `NOTE_MIN_MS` and less than `CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS`.
- The ledger's F2 rows run undirected and without rising tempo or late montage, so they don't show what the app plays.
  Directed, Pulsar gets *longer*.
- The new constant has no 15 row.
- 15 §8's effect inventory still describes the old jump-in.

## Checks run (this review)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run -s typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `npm run -s lint` | exit 0 |
| `npm test` | 110 files, 1729 tests passed |
| `npm run e2e:spec -- gallery-summon` | 1 passed (18.4 s) |
| `npm run e2e:spec -- solar-dense montage-names` (not run by the builder) | all passed (see the tail of this file) |
| F2's `BUILT` rows re-run directed with rising tempo and late montage (a scratch script in `/tmp`, not committed) | Comet 0.3, Nova 2.3, Quasar 7.3, **Pulsar −1.8**, Convoy 7.0, Harbor 3.3, **Meteor 1.3** s saved |
| The same, undirected with rising tempo and late montage | Comet 0.3, Nova 2.3, Quasar 16.5, Pulsar 18.9, Convoy 7.0, Harbor 3.3, Meteor 34.3 (the same savings as the committed rows; only the absolute lengths differ) |

## Acceptance, line by line

| Acceptance | Met? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Gallery demo cell, full and reduced motion, no console errors | Yes | `gallery-summon.spec.ts` passes. The `agentStillMs`, `agentTravel` and `reducedAgentTravel` stats are wired correctly (`maneuverDemos.ts` `trackAgent`; reset per loop; reduced-only loops gated by `reducedAll`). |
| Unit test: no hold between the flight and the next place; the act within 50 ms of the blip | Yes | `summonOnTheFly.test.ts` passes. The blip and `cmd.act(f.key,'jump')` come from the same `act` phase call (`stationJumpIn.ts:44-58`), so they share a frame. |
| 15 §7 row and `docTables.test.ts` | Yes for §7 (2515; matches `spanMs`). **Partly** for the rest of 15 | See M3 and M4. |
| Schedule goldens updated, and the packet names each change | Updated, but **misnamed** | See m3. |
| The ledger shows the saving per pod | Shows *a* saving per pod, but not what the app plays | See M2. |
| Decided: plate rides with the ship for `NOTE_MIN_MS` | **No** (whole only 1.28 s) | See M1. |

## Findings

### M1 (Major): the passing plate is whole for 1280 ms, under `NOTE_MIN_MS` (1800) and `CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS` (1500)
- **Where:** `src/renderer/src/chart/fx/movers.ts:348` (`crewOpen`), `src/renderer/src/theme/starChart/maneuvers/stationJumpIn.ts:27,37`
  (`rideS: PASS_PLATE_MS`), and `src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:809`.
- **Evidence:**
  - `PASS_PLATE_MS = CREW_FOLD_MS + NOTE_MIN_MS` = 2320, documented as "its unfurl and the least time it is read".
  - `Sortie.crewOpen` returns `min(h/fold, (open − h)/fold)` with `open = rideS` = 2.32 s, so the *fold* is inside
    the 2.32 s as well. The plate unfurls over 0–0.52 s, is whole over 0.52–1.80 s (**1.28 s**), and folds over
    1.80–2.32 s.
  - The interpreter sets the label window to `[openMs, openMs + PASS_PLATE_MS]` (`interpreter.ts:620`), which would
    give 1.8 s whole with the fold after it. But `castLabels.crew` prefers the flown value (`open = flown ?? own`), so
    the Sortie's shorter opening wins.
  - 15 §10 defines both minima as times the plate is "whole (not unfurling or folding)", and R14 says "held long
    enough to read". The unit test only checks `u > 0` for at least 1760 ms (2320 passes), so it doesn't catch this.
- **Fix:** let a pass's plate stay whole for `NOTE_MIN_MS` (at least `CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS`) and then fold. For example,
  `rideS = (2·CREW_FOLD_MS + NOTE_MIN_MS)/1000`, or have `crewOpen` treat `rideS` as the start of the fold. Keep the
  leg on at least as long, so the plate doesn't ride a parked ship. Set the interpreter's `closeMs` to match.
  Optionally, tighten the unit test to measure `u === 1` time.

### M2 (Major): F2's ledger rows don't show the saving the app plays, and the ledger doesn't say so
- **Where:** `scripts/pacing-built.ts:158-170` (the F2 entry), and the rows in `docs/progress/v1.4/pacing-ledger.md:575-581`.
- **Evidence:**
  - The entry has no `directs`, `rises` or `late`. Both runs are therefore undirected, without rising tempo (E8), and
    without late-day montage (E10). The comment says "Now: today's rules", which is not true.
  - The builder's reason for running undirected is honest in `build.md`: directed, the budget fit re-spends the saving.
    My re-run confirms that with today's directed rules, Pulsar is **1.8 s longer** with F2, Meteor saves 1.3 s (not
    34.3), and Quasar saves 7.3 s (not 16.5). The director golden agrees: one speed pod's `estimateMs` rises
    296189 → 296950.
  - The ledger itself publishes only the undirected 18.9 s for Pulsar and 34.3 s for Meteor, with no note.
  - 27 Decisions 2026-11-01 (E5a review-1) and 2026-11-06 (block E audit) ask that the ledger describe the app's
    schedule. The ahead-written test's `savedMs ≥ 0` makes the directed figure untestable as written, so it isn't only
    the builder's choice. The rows still read as the user-facing saving.
- **Fix:**
  - At least, correct the comment and add an F2 note to the ledger's Built section: "undirected, recorded time, the
    rule's own saving; directed the budget fit re-spends it: Pulsar −1.8 s, Meteor 1.3 s, …".
  - Better, also record a directed row set (a separate id such as `F2d`, exempt from `savedMs ≥ 0`) so the final
    check sees the real effect.
  - Set `rises: true, late: true` so "now" is today's rules. The savings don't change; I checked.

### M3 (Major): new constant `PASS_PLATE_MS` has no 15 §10 row
- **Where:** `src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:809`, and `docs/15-reference.md` §10 (rows 1256–1259 hold
  `NOTE_MIN_MS`, `CREW_HOLD_MS`, `CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS` and `CREW_FOLD_MS`; the derived `VOLLEY_TURN_MS` has its own row at
  1218).
- **Evidence:** CLAUDE.md says "Change a constant and its row in the same change". `docTables` passes only because §10's
  check doesn't enumerate it.
- **Fix:**
  - Add a row: "A pass's plate (new, 27 F2) | 2320 ms (or the M1-corrected value) | `@shared/engine/maneuvers.ts`
    PASS_PLATE_MS | …".
  - Amend the `CREW_HOLD_MS` row ("Their sortie holds that long, and the planner counts it (`durMs`)") to note that a
    passing rule (`passes`) holds no turn.
  - Amend the `CREW_FOLD_MS` row ("once the ship is parked") for the pass.

### M4 (Major): 15 §8's effect inventory still lists the retired jump-in effects and omits the blip
- **Where:** `docs/15-reference.md:956-963`.
- **Evidence:**
  - Line 956 still lists "Station jump-in | tell | `ring` closing on the station's spot | … | keep", but the tell is gone
    from the code and the rule.
  - Line 959 still lists the gather's `ring` fold ("mutes first"), which `stationJumpIn.ts` no longer issues.
  - There's no row for the act's call blip (`ring` at the passing ship), which is the item's main new effect.
  - The table is 15's authority on what each effect is for. The diff updated §7, 13 §6 and 05 §8 but not this table.
- **Fix:** remove or mark as cut the tell and fold rows, citing 27 F2. Add "Station jump-in | act | `ring` call blip at
  the passing ship, At-rest blue, the arrival's shape | Who summoned it, and that the arrival is its effect | — | 0 |
  keep". Also update the `pursue` row at 884 ("a sortie out, a hold and home") to cover a pass.

### m1 (Minor): the plate outlives the jump-in's attention hold by about 520 ms
- **Where:** `src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:621` (`heldMs`) against `movers.ts:348`.
- **Evidence:**
  - `heldMs = max(durMs, NOTE_MIN_MS)` = 2515 from the start, so the places are held from the claim (715) to 2515.
  - The plate shows from 715 to 3035.
  - Before F2, `durMs` was stretched to `leaveMs`, which covered the plate.
  - A neighbour placed by the budget at 2515 can now overlap a still-visible summoner plate (R14, ATTENTION_MAX). The
    renderer's `hasRoom` mitigates this but doesn't prevent it for windows already issued.
- **Fix:** for a passing rule, hold the places to `claim + PASS_PLATE_MS (+ fold)`, for example through `heldMs`.
  Re-run the goldens if the length moves.

### m2 (Minor): R8's tension isn't recorded
- **Where:** `docs/13-game-design.md:50` (R8: "movement and interaction never blur into one").
- **Evidence:** F2 deliberately interacts while moving (the user's Decided), and 13 §6 cites R8 and R10 in support. R8
  as written forbids it, and there's no note of the exception.
- **Fix:** add one clause to R8, or to the 13 §6 row: "a summons may be given in passing (27 F2)".

### m3 (Minor): build.md misnames two of the golden changes
- **Where:** `docs/progress/v1.4/work/F2/build.md`, *Golden changes*.
- **Evidence:**
  - It says "Pulsar 296189 → 296950 and tempo 1.9 → 1.8", but in `tests/golden/__golden__/director.json` that entry
    (line 35) is **Quasar Pod**.
  - It says "Quasar-side pod (second speed pod) 294434 → 284444, tempo 1.1 → 1.05", but that entry (line 65) is
    **Pulsar Pod**.
  - The acceptance requires the packet to name each change.
- **Fix:** swap the names, and say plainly that Quasar's directed estimate *grows* by 0.76 s.

### m4 (Minor): 05 §8 T-1 still says the station "jumps in where its summoner waits"
- **Where:** `docs/05-playback.md:833`.
- **Evidence:** the summoner no longer waits.
- **Fix:** "… it jumps in as its summoner passes (27 F2) …".

### m5 (Minor): `releaseOfPlay` reads the global `PACE_RULES`, not the plan's rules
- **Where:** `src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:802-803`.
- **Evidence:**
  - The planner's `releaseOf` reads `d.rule.passes`, which respects custom `rules`, such as `withoutSummonOnTheFly`.
  - `releaseOfPlay` (and so `nearWaits`) always treats `facility.enter` as passing.
  - That's harmless in the app, which uses `PACE_RULES`. It's inconsistent for any caller that plans with substituted
    rules.
  - It also duplicates `flyingPlay`'s lookup.
- **Fix:** share one lookup helper (as `ruleById` is in the interpreter), or document the assumption.

### n1 (Nit): `sweep.test.ts:171` comment
"Comet's length as E7 measured it … less the 300 ms" now pins a post-F2 value. That's fine, but the earlier items
otherwise undo F2 through `withoutSummonOnTheFly`. Either run this check with that helper, so the E7 number stays
61_845, or keep it as is. The justification in build.md holds either way.

### n2 (Nit): build.md's leg-on speed
build.md says "fast in, slower out; accepted". There's a speed discontinuity at the pass: ease-in arrives at about 2×
the average speed, and ease-out leaves at about 2× the leg-on's average over a 2.3 s leg. It's worth a look in
`npm run gallery`. It isn't wrong.

### n3 (Nit): naming
`Sortie`'s `pass` mode shares a word with the Strike run's "sortie as a pass" (13 §6). A name like `through` or
`onTheFly` would avoid confusion.

## Things checked and found sound
- **Edited tests:**
  - `commands.test.ts` replaces the fold-ring assertion with stronger ones (no rings in the gather, no `holdS`,
    `rideS > 0`, and an act with blip plus arrival). That's justified.
  - `sweep.test.ts` changes a pinned length by exactly the removed tell (300 ms), which is consistent with Comet's
    ledger row.
  - The committed F2 tests and `pacingBuilt` frozen rows are untouched in this diff. The `F*` filter is in a985a15, the

- **Director/`ARRIVING`:** summons stay unprotected and outside `ARRIVING`, as the item leaves them. `crewBusy`/

# F2 Summon on the fly: review 1

Reviewer: fresh, adversarial. Reviewed the uncommitted working-tree diff on `bench` against the tests in a985a15, the item
F2 (27), 02 §1, 13 §1 (R1–R14), 13 §6, 15 §7/§8/§10, 05 §8, tests.md and build.md. Fixture data only (INV-18).

## Verdict: **changes requested** (1 Blocker, 3 Majors, 5 Minors, 3 Nits)

The choreography does what the item asks. The pass has no hold, there's one blip at the passing ship with the station's
`jump` at the same instant, and the hue and `r1/r` match. Reduced motion plays both at the ship's rest. The engine no
longer stretches the jump-in by the crew hold. The edits to existing tests are justified. The problems:

- **An existing e2e spec fails with this diff and passes at HEAD** (B1): the plate is whole for less than `NOTE_MIN_MS`
  and less than `CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS`, and the spec's "parked while named" check conflicts with the item's design. The
  builder didn't run `solar-dense` or the full e2e suite.
- The ledger's F2 rows run undirected and without rising tempo or late montage, so they don't show what the app plays.
  Directed, Pulsar gets *longer*.
- The new constant has no 15 row.
- 15 §8's effect inventory still describes the old jump-in.

## Checks run (this review)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run -s typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `npm run -s lint` | exit 0 |
| `npm test` | 110 files, 1729 tests passed |
| `npm run e2e:spec -- gallery-summon` | 1 passed (18.4 s) |
| `npm run e2e:spec -- solar-dense montage-names` (not run by the builder) | 12 passed, **1 failed**, 11 did not run: `solar-dense.spec.ts:400` *a captain's turn: named once parked, held a second past the work…* fails at `:459` with `Expected: > 1400, Received: 1202`. A second run gave 1151. |
| The same spec at HEAD (a985a15, in a temporary detached worktree, since removed) | **passed**, so F2 causes the failure |
| F2's `BUILT` rows re-run directed with rising tempo and late montage (a scratch script in `/tmp`, not committed) | Comet 0.3, Nova 2.3, Quasar 7.3, **Pulsar −1.8**, Convoy 7.0, Harbor 3.3, **Meteor 1.3** s saved |
| The same, undirected with rising tempo and late montage | Comet 0.3, Nova 2.3, Quasar 16.5, Pulsar 18.9, Convoy 7.0, Harbor 3.3, Meteor 34.3 (the same savings as the committed rows; only the absolute lengths differ) |

## Acceptance, line by line

| Acceptance | Met? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Gallery demo cell, full and reduced motion, no console errors | Yes | `gallery-summon.spec.ts` passes. The `agentStillMs`, `agentTravel` and `reducedAgentTravel` stats are wired correctly (`maneuverDemos.ts` `trackAgent`; reset per loop; reduced-only loops gated by `reducedAll`). |
| Unit test: no hold between the flight and the next place; the act within 50 ms of the blip | Yes | `summonOnTheFly.test.ts` passes. The blip and `cmd.act(f.key,'jump')` come from the same `act` phase call (`stationJumpIn.ts:44-58`), so they share a frame. |
| 15 §7 row and `docTables.test.ts` | Yes for §7 (2515; matches `spanMs`). **Partly** for the rest of 15 | See M3 and M4. |
| Schedule goldens updated, and the packet names each change | Updated, but **misnamed** | See m3. |
| The ledger shows the saving per pod | Shows *a* saving per pod, but not what the app plays | See M2. |
| Decided: plate rides with the ship for `NOTE_MIN_MS` | **No** (whole only 1.28 s; an existing e2e spec fails) | See B1. |

## Findings

### B1 (Blocker): `solar-dense.spec.ts:400` fails; the passing plate is whole for 1280 ms, under `NOTE_MIN_MS` (1800) and `CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS` (1500)
- **Regression:** the existing e2e spec *a captain's turn: named once parked…* (`tests/e2e/solar-dense.spec.ts:459`)
  measures each acting plate's whole time. It got 1202 and 1151 ms in two runs, against a required > 1400. It passes at
  HEAD.
- **A second conflict:** its next assertion (`:461`, "Parked while named: moved < 12" screen px) contradicts F2's
  Decided ("its plate rides with the ship"). Once the whole time is fixed, a passing summoner will fail it too.
- **That spec needs a justified edit:** exempt `facility.enter` passes from the parked check, or assert that passes
  ride. Record the edit in the build's *Changes to existing tests*.
- **Where:** `src/renderer/src/chart/fx/movers.ts:348` (`crewOpen`), `src/renderer/src/theme/starChart/maneuvers/stationJumpIn.ts:27,37`
  (`rideS: PASS_PLATE_MS`), and `src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:809`.
- **Evidence:**
  - `PASS_PLATE_MS = CREW_FOLD_MS + NOTE_MIN_MS` = 2320, documented as "its unfurl and the least time it is read".
  - `Sortie.crewOpen` returns `min(h/fold, (open − h)/fold)` with `open = rideS` = 2.32 s, so the *fold* is inside
    the 2.32 s as well. The plate unfurls over 0–0.52 s, is whole over 0.52–1.80 s (**1.28 s**), and folds over
    1.80–2.32 s.
  - The interpreter sets the label window to `[openMs, openMs + PASS_PLATE_MS]` (`interpreter.ts:620`), which would
    give 1.8 s whole with the fold after it. But `castLabels.crew` prefers the flown value (`open = flown ?? own`), so
    the Sortie's shorter opening wins.
  - 15 §10 defines both minima as times the plate is "whole (not unfurling or folding)", and R14 says "held long
    enough to read". The unit test only checks `u > 0` for at least 1760 ms (2320 passes), so it doesn't catch this.
- **Fix:** let a pass's plate stay whole for `NOTE_MIN_MS` (at least `CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS`) and then fold. For example,
  `rideS = (2·CREW_FOLD_MS + NOTE_MIN_MS)/1000`, or have `crewOpen` treat `rideS` as the start of the fold. Keep the
  leg on at least as long, so the plate doesn't ride a parked ship. Set the interpreter's `closeMs` to match.
  Optionally, tighten the unit test to measure `u === 1` time.

### M2 (Major): F2's ledger rows don't show the saving the app plays, and the ledger doesn't say so
- **Where:** `scripts/pacing-built.ts:158-170` (the F2 entry), and the rows in `docs/progress/v1.4/pacing-ledger.md:575-581`.
- **Evidence:**
  - The entry has no `directs`, `rises` or `late`. Both runs are therefore undirected, without rising tempo (E8), and
    without late-day montage (E10). The comment says "Now: today's rules", which is not true.
  - The builder's reason for running undirected is honest in `build.md`: directed, the budget fit re-spends the saving.
    My re-run confirms that with today's directed rules, Pulsar is **1.8 s longer** with F2, Meteor saves 1.3 s (not
    34.3), and Quasar saves 7.3 s (not 16.5). The director golden agrees: one speed pod's `estimateMs` rises
    296189 → 296950.
  - The ledger itself publishes only the undirected 18.9 s for Pulsar and 34.3 s for Meteor, with no note.
  - 27 Decisions 2026-11-01 (E5a review-1) and 2026-11-06 (block E audit) ask that the ledger describe the app's
    schedule. The ahead-written test's `savedMs ≥ 0` makes the directed figure untestable as written, so it isn't only
    the builder's choice. The rows still read as the user-facing saving.
- **Fix:**
  - At least, correct the comment and add an F2 note to the ledger's Built section: "undirected, recorded time, the
    rule's own saving; directed the budget fit re-spends it: Pulsar −1.8 s, Meteor 1.3 s, …".
  - Better, also record a directed row set (a separate id such as `F2d`, exempt from `savedMs ≥ 0`) so the final
    check sees the real effect.
  - Set `rises: true, late: true` so "now" is today's rules. The savings don't change; I checked.

### M3 (Major): new constant `PASS_PLATE_MS` has no 15 §10 row
- **Where:** `src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:809`, and `docs/15-reference.md` §10 (rows 1256–1259 hold
  `NOTE_MIN_MS`, `CREW_HOLD_MS`, `CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS` and `CREW_FOLD_MS`; the derived `VOLLEY_TURN_MS` has its own row at
  1218).
- **Evidence:** CLAUDE.md says "Change a constant and its row in the same change". `docTables` passes only because §10's
  check doesn't enumerate it.
- **Fix:**
  - Add a row: "A pass's plate (new, 27 F2) | 2320 ms (or the B1-corrected value) | `@shared/engine/maneuvers.ts`
    PASS_PLATE_MS | …".
  - Amend the `CREW_HOLD_MS` row ("Their sortie holds that long, and the planner counts it (`durMs`)") to note that a
    passing rule (`passes`) holds no turn.
  - Amend the `CREW_FOLD_MS` row ("once the ship is parked") for the pass.

### M4 (Major): 15 §8's effect inventory still lists the retired jump-in effects and omits the blip
- **Where:** `docs/15-reference.md:956-963`.
- **Evidence:**
  - Line 956 still lists "Station jump-in | tell | `ring` closing on the station's spot | … | keep", but the tell is gone
    from the code and the rule.
  - Line 959 still lists the gather's `ring` fold ("mutes first"), which `stationJumpIn.ts` no longer issues.
  - There's no row for the act's call blip (`ring` at the passing ship), which is the item's main new effect.
  - The table is 15's authority on what each effect is for. The diff updated §7, 13 §6 and 05 §8 but not this table.
- **Fix:** remove or mark as cut the tell and fold rows, citing 27 F2. Add "Station jump-in | act | `ring` call blip at
  the passing ship, At-rest blue, the arrival's shape | Who summoned it, and that the arrival is its effect | — | 0 |
  keep". Also update the `pursue` row at 884 ("a sortie out, a hold and home") to cover a pass.

### m1 (Minor): the plate outlives the jump-in's attention hold by about 520 ms
- **Where:** `src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:621` (`heldMs`) against `movers.ts:348`.
- **Evidence:**
  - `heldMs = max(durMs, NOTE_MIN_MS)` = 2515 from the start, so the places are held from the claim (715) to 2515.
  - The plate shows from 715 to 3035.
  - Before F2, `durMs` was stretched to `leaveMs`, which covered the plate.
  - A neighbour placed by the budget at 2515 can now overlap a still-visible summoner plate (R14, ATTENTION_MAX). The
    renderer's `hasRoom` mitigates this but doesn't prevent it for windows already issued.
- **Fix:** for a passing rule, hold the places to `claim + PASS_PLATE_MS (+ fold)`, for example through `heldMs`.
  Re-run the goldens if the length moves.

### m2 (Minor): R8's tension isn't recorded
- **Where:** `docs/13-game-design.md:50` (R8: "movement and interaction never blur into one").
- **Evidence:** F2 deliberately interacts while moving (the user's Decided), and 13 §6 cites R8 and R10 in support. R8
  as written forbids it, and there's no note of the exception.
- **Fix:** add one clause to R8, or to the 13 §6 row: "a summons may be given in passing (27 F2)".

### m3 (Minor): build.md misnames two of the golden changes
- **Where:** `docs/progress/v1.4/work/F2/build.md`, *Golden changes*.
- **Evidence:**
  - It says "Pulsar 296189 → 296950 and tempo 1.9 → 1.8", but in `tests/golden/__golden__/director.json` that entry
    (line 35) is **Quasar Pod**.
  - It says "Quasar-side pod (second speed pod) 294434 → 284444, tempo 1.1 → 1.05", but that entry (line 65) is
    **Pulsar Pod**.
  - The acceptance requires the packet to name each change.
- **Fix:** swap the names, and say plainly that Quasar's directed estimate *grows* by 0.76 s.

### m4 (Minor): 05 §8 T-1 still says the station "jumps in where its summoner waits"
- **Where:** `docs/05-playback.md:833`.
- **Evidence:** the summoner no longer waits.
- **Fix:** "… it jumps in as its summoner passes (27 F2) …".

### m5 (Minor): `releaseOfPlay` reads the global `PACE_RULES`, not the plan's rules
- **Where:** `src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:802-803`.
- **Evidence:**
  - The planner's `releaseOf` reads `d.rule.passes`, which respects custom `rules`, such as `withoutSummonOnTheFly`.
  - `releaseOfPlay` (and so `nearWaits`) always treats `facility.enter` as passing.
  - That's harmless in the app, which uses `PACE_RULES`. It's inconsistent for any caller that plans with substituted
    rules.
  - It also duplicates `flyingPlay`'s lookup.
- **Fix:** share one lookup helper (as `ruleById` is in the interpreter), or document the assumption.

### n1 (Nit): `sweep.test.ts:171` comment
"Comet's length as E7 measured it … less the 300 ms" now pins a post-F2 value. That's fine, but the earlier items
otherwise undo F2 through `withoutSummonOnTheFly`. Either run this check with that helper, so the E7 number stays
61_845, or keep it as is. The justification in build.md holds either way.

### n2 (Nit): build.md's leg-on speed
build.md says "fast in, slower out; accepted". There's a speed discontinuity at the pass: ease-in arrives at about 2×
the average speed, and ease-out leaves at about 2× the leg-on's average over a 2.3 s leg. It's worth a look in
`npm run gallery`. It isn't wrong.

### n3 (Nit): naming
`Sortie`'s `pass` mode shares a word with the Strike run's "sortie as a pass" (13 §6). A name like `through` or
`onTheFly` would avoid confusion.

## Things checked and found sound
- **Edited tests:**
  - `commands.test.ts` replaces the fold-ring assertion with stronger ones (no rings in the gather, no `holdS`,
    `rideS > 0`, and an act with blip plus arrival). That's justified.
  - `sweep.test.ts` changes a pinned length by exactly the removed tell (300 ms), which is consistent with Comet's
    ledger row.
  - The committed F2 tests and `pacingBuilt` frozen rows are untouched in this diff. The `F*` filter is in a985a15, the
    test author's Decision 8.
- **Frozen earlier rows:** they hold honestly. `withoutSummonOnTheFly` restores E1's phases and drops `passes`, so
  `holdsCrew` and `releaseOf` behave as before.
- **`src/shared` purity:** no new imports in `pace.ts` or `maneuvers.ts`.
- **Pixi:** no Pixi API in the diff (the gallery stats read `scene.liveOf` only).
- **Other `Sortie`/`pursue` users:** `pass` defaults to `null`, `arc`'s ease defaults to `easeInOut`, and the end
  condition and `crewOpen` are unchanged when `pass` is null. `solar-dense` and `montage-names` pass. Per the build,
  `solar-play` and the keystone pass too.
- **Reduced motion:** `pursue` snaps, so the blip is drawn at the ship's live anchor (its rest), with the arrival in the
  same act call. This is covered by the unit test and the e2e test.
- **Director/`ARRIVING`:** summons stay unprotected and outside `ARRIVING`, as the item leaves them. `crewBusy`/
  `nearStartMs` floor the next flying turn at the jump-in's work end (2515), so a P4 takeover doesn't cut the plate
  before `claim + 1800`.
- **Goldens:** only `director.json` moved. `npm run fixtures` moved no layout or v0 golden (per the build; consistent
  with the diff).
# F2 Summon on the fly: build record

Not committed (the orchestrator commits). Fixture data only (INV-18).

## What changed (files)

- `src/shared/engine/pace.ts`: `PaceRule.passes` (a rule whose crew ships pass through the work without stopping);
  `facility.enter` is `passes: true`, phases `gather 715, act 1200, land 600` (2515 ms; no tell).
- `src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts`: a passing rule holds no crew turn (`holdsCrew`): its `durMs` is its phases, and its
  ships are released at the act's start (`releaseOf`, and `releaseOfPlay`, which now reads `id` to find the rule).
  New `PASS_PLATE_MS` (= `CREW_FOLD_MS + NOTE_MIN_MS`): how long the passing ship's plate shows.
- `src/renderer/src/chart/fx/movers.ts` (`Sortie`): a `pass` mode. It speeds into the spot (ease-in), gives no hold, and
  slows on to its next place (ease-out) over `max(backS, waitS + 0.4)`, so a waiting P4 sortie takes the ship over while
  it is still moving; its plate (`crewOpen`) rides for `rideS`.
- `src/renderer/src/chart/fx/commands.ts`: `PursueArgs.rideS` turns a sortie into a pass.
- `src/renderer/src/chart/fx/v1/interpreter.ts`: a passing rule's crew plate opens at the act and shuts `PASS_PLATE_MS` later.
- `src/renderer/src/theme/starChart/maneuvers/stationJumpIn.ts`: no tell, no fold-ring repeat, no hold or fly-back. The act
  gives one call blip (a ring on the passing ship, `HERO_GLOW`, the arrival ring's `0.7 -> 1.6` shape) with the station's
  `jump` act, flare and ring at the same instant. A guest (no ship here) still drops in at the spot.
- `src/renderer/src/gallery/maneuverDemos.ts`: `agentStillMs`, `agentTravel`, `reducedAgentTravel` on every demo's stats.
- `scripts/pacing-built.ts`: `BUILT` entry `F2` (all seven pods, undirected, before = E1's jump-in); the earlier items now
  run both schedules with E1's jump-in (`withoutSummonOnTheFly`), as E7/E8/E10 do for theirs, so their frozen rows hold.
- Docs: `docs/15-reference.md` §7 row (2515, what you see), `docs/13-game-design.md` §6 row, `docs/05-playback.md` §8 M-13 row.
- Regenerated (`npm run pacing -- --candidates`): `docs/progress/v1.4/pacing-ledger.{md,json}`, `pacing-built.json`,
  `pacing-candidates.json`.

## Decisions
